body:
@bbarry In that example, the `ngTemplateGuard_ngLet: 'binding';` seems inappropriate to me, as the directly doesn't conditionally render the template, so the `ngLet` input's expression should not be used as guard. If that is done, you'd remove all falsy types from the expression within the template, which would be incorrect.

Your `ngTemplateContextGuard` has a return type that specifies `ctx is NgLetDirective<T>`, I would assume you meant to type `ctx is NgLetContext<T>`
Status: Docs team will need some guidance on how to update the doc.
Hi @bbarry, the language service is currently being updated to work identically to the real compilation, including type guards. This is still work in progress and not yet available.
